claims.claim: A graph G has a radius-one neighbor with a triangle partition if and only if V(G) has a partition into triples each spanning at least two edges of G; moreover, a positive output may use additions only.
claims.evidence: The symmetric-difference graph has maximum degree at most one, hence its edges form a matching. Two H-edges missing from G inside one H-triangle would share a vertex and give edit degree two, so every factor triple spans at least two G-edges. Conversely, adding the sole missing edge of each deficient triple works, and the additions form a matching because the triples are disjoint. Exhaustive checks confirmed the equivalence for every graph of orders 0, 3, and 6 and every radius-one edit.
claims.search_method: Direct proof from the distance definition plus exhaustive exact bitmask enumeration.

claims.claim: Every radius-one negative output can be replaced by one obtained solely by deleting a matching from G.
claims.evidence: Write H=(G-D)+A, where A∪D is the edit matching. Then H0=G-D=H-A is a subgraph of H. If H0 had a triangle partition, the same partition would exist in H, contradicting negativity. Thus H0 is negative and differs from G only by the matching D. The checker confirmed this for all 2,178,340 negative radius-one pairs at orders 0, 3, and 6.
claims.search_method: Monotonicity proof plus exhaustive enumeration of every small graph/edit pair.

claims.claim: There is a polynomially checkable modulo-three separator certificate for negative outputs.
claims.evidence: In any triangle partition, all vertices of a factor triangle outside X lie in one component of T(H)-X, because their mutual edge belongs to T(H). A component whose order is nonzero modulo three therefore needs a distinct factor triangle crossing into X. Such triangles are disjoint and each consumes an X-vertex, so their number is at most |X|. Hence q>|X| soundly proves nonexistence. Constructing T(H), its components, and q is polynomial. This verifies the stated sound certificate; it does not assert completeness for every no-instance. Exhaustive checking found no violation among all H and X at orders 0, 3, and 6.
claims.search_method: Component-congruence proof plus exhaustive evaluation of every separator set X on all small graphs.

claims.claim: If S⊆V satisfies |S|>n/3 and Δ(G[S])≤1, then a valid negative output is constructible in polynomial time from S.
claims.evidence: The edges of G[S] form a matching. Deleting them makes S independent while respecting radius one. Every resulting triangle contains at most one vertex of S, so n/3 disjoint triangles cannot cover more than n/3 vertices of S, contradicting |S|>n/3. The checker validated all 409,576 qualifying (G,S) pairs at orders 0, 3, and 6.
claims.search_method: Direct counting proof plus exhaustive enumeration of all qualifying vertex subsets.

claims.claim: A greedy polynomial algorithm resolves every input except possibly when it leaves between 1 and n/3 vertices.
claims.evidence: Each removed triple consists of a center and two current neighbors, hence spans at least two original edges. At termination the remainder R has maximum degree at most one. If R is empty, Claim 0 constructs a positive output; if |R|>n/3, Claim 3 constructs a negative output. Each iteration removes three vertices, so the procedure is polynomial and the only untreated case is 0<|R|≤n/3. Exact execution on every graph of orders 0, 3, and 6 confirmed all invariants and constructed outputs.
claims.search_method: Invariant and termination proof plus exhaustive execution of a deterministic lowest-label greedy implementation.

claims.claim: Given X with |X|<n/3 and Δ(G-X)≤3, a valid negative output can be constructed in polynomial time. Consequently this applies whenever fewer than n/3 vertices of G have degree at least four.
claims.evidence: A cut locally maximal under single-vertex flips is found by strictly increasing the integer cut size. At termination each residual vertex has at most as many same-side as cross-side neighbors; residual degree at most three therefore gives at most one same-side neighbor. The monochromatic edges form a matching. Deleting them makes H-X bipartite, so every H-triangle meets X, whereas a triangle partition would require n/3 distinct X-vertices. Taking X as the vertices of G-degree at least four satisfies the residual-degree premise. Exact checks covered 159,532 qualifying (G,X) instances and 22,744 corollary instances at orders 0, 3, and 6.
claims.search_method: Local-cut potential proof plus exhaustive construction for all qualifying small instances.

claims.claim: There is a polynomially recognizable dense-side condition producing a positive output.
claims.evidence: The stated condition is valid: let C contain vertices with at least two nonneighbors and L=V-C, require |C|≤n/3, and find a matching saturating two clones of every c∈C into L. Each c and its two matched G-neighbors form a good triple. Every remaining L-vertex has at most one nonneighbor, so every arbitrary triple of unused L misses at most one edge. These triples cover V, and their missing edges form a matching. Clone matching and the construction are polynomial. The checker validated all 1,341 satisfying graphs at orders 0, 3, and 6.
claims.search_method: Constructive clone-matching proof plus exhaustive recognition and output validation on all small graphs.
claims.witness: The condition C={v:d_complement(G)(v)≥2}, L=V-C, |C|≤n/3, with a matching saturating two clones of each c into L.

claims.claim: The complete target is solvable for n=0,3,6.
claims.evidence: The greedy remainder has order divisible by three. For n=3 or 6, every nonempty remainder has at least three vertices, which is strictly greater than n/3, so the negative branch applies; an empty remainder gives the positive branch. The empty partition handles n=0. Exhaustive checking resolved all 1+8+32,768 labeled graphs, with 14,731 positive and 18,046 negative constructed outputs and no unresolved case.
claims.search_method: Divisibility argument plus exhaustive exact verification of every labeled graph at the three claimed orders.

claims.claim: For every integer a≥2 there is a connected, triangle-support-connected graph W_a of order 3(5a+2) having no P3/triangle factor although its largest induced subgraph of maximum degree one has only 10<n/3 vertices.
claims.evidence: For W_a, the order is 1+5(3a+1)=3(5a+2). Every edge belongs to a triangle, and the universal vertex z connects the graph, so its triangle-support graph is connected. A good triple avoiding z must lie inside one clique. The unique triple containing z touches at most two cliques, leaving at least three untouched cliques of order 1 modulo three, which cannot be covered internally. A dissociation set containing z has size at most two; one avoiding z contains at most two vertices per clique, giving the exact maximum 10, attained by choosing two from each clique. Since n/3=5a+2≥12, 10<n/3. The checker exactly confirmed the smallest member W_2 and all its category-count states.
claims.search_method: Uniform structural and modular proof, supplemented by exact category-state enumeration for W_2 and integer formula checks.
claims.witness: W_a consists of one vertex z joined to all vertices of five pairwise anticomplete cliques C_i, each of order 3a+1.

claims.claim: The family W_a also shows that restricting the negative branch to making the graph triangle-free by a matching deletion is insufficient, while the separator certificate detects its negative answer.
claims.evidence: Every clique C_i contains a K7. For any matching deletion, its restriction to that K7 is a matching; choosing one vertex from each of three distinct deleted-pair/singleton blocks gives a surviving triangle. Thus no matching deletion makes W_a triangle-free. On the other hand every edge of W_a is triangle-supported, so T(W_a)-{z} has exactly five components of order 3a+1≡1 mod 3. Hence q=5>|{z}|=1 certifies the negative output H=W_a. The checker exhaustively tested all 232 K7 matchings and computed q=5 for W_2.
claims.search_method: Uniform clique-core proof and exact separator calculation, supplemented by exhaustive enumeration of every K7 matching.
claims.witness: The family W_a from Claim 8, using the unchanged negative output H=W_a and separator X={z}.

target_evidence: The exact target requests a total polynomial-time construction for every graph of order divisible by three, or a rigorous disproof of that exact FP membership claim. The draft supplies correct and material normal forms, several polynomial positive and negative branches, a complete solution for n=0,3,6, and counterexamples to two tempting sufficient dichotomies, but it neither proves that its branches cover every graph nor disproves membership. Therefore it is VALID_PARTIAL_PROGRESS rather than a full resolution. Its claimed_resolution is PARTIAL, and the final writeup expressly says the general claim remains unresolved and makes no membership or hardness claim, so that resolution label is ACCURATE.
